title: Ephemeral snapshot prober for staged weight and KV priming
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a low-cost, low-latency approach to mitigate cold-starts for dedicated capacity fleets by prewarming both model weights and KV caches using transient probing agents ("ephemeral snapshot probers"). Instead of simply keeping full warm replicas running, this work implements lightweight, bandwidth-efficient probes that bring just-enough state into local memory and GPU resident caches to make the first few requests fast while minimizing reserved capacity cost.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Reduce 95th percentile cold-start latency (first-token) for typical 7B and 13B models by >= 60% compared to baseline cold path.
- Added runtime cost of probes <= 3% of committed fleet CPU/GPU time in steady state.
- No increase in tail error rates or degraded throughput for warm requests.
- Rolloutable via feature flag per-tenant and per-pool; observable via new Grafana panels.

Design overview:
1) Ephemeral probe agents: short-lived containers co-located with serving nodes that perform a staged fetch of the model checkpoint in micro-shards. They use memory-mapped reads and OS prefetch (madvise/MAP_POPULATE where available) to trigger page faults in a controlled order. For GPU loading, probes trigger the runtime's weight streaming path with a special "probe" mode that loads quantized shards into GPU memory without registering a full serving endpoint.

2) KV priming strategy: probes issue a set of synthetic prefix requests designed to exercise the model's KV layout (typical prefix sequences representative of tenant workload) to populate local KV caches and the runtime's KV store. Probes maintain a small, rotating prompt set per-tenant sourced from anonymized real traffic or curated seeds.

3) Progressive weight streaming: rather than pulling full precision weights, probes pull a lightweight quantized overlay (e.g., 8-bit or 4-bit shards) sufficient for low-latency warmup. If a live request arrives requiring higher precision, the runtime upgrades the relevant shards progressively.

4) Residency and eviction scoring: integrate with the fleet controller to track probe-driven residency scores per model/tenant. Scoring informs warm-pool prioritization and eviction policies (least-recently-probed across low-priority tenants).

5) Safety and isolation: probes run under service accounts with limited privileges and advertise no public endpoints. They are feature-flag controlled and tenant opt-in. Probes obey memory caps and must not evict production serving pages by causing pressure spikes.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full warm replicas give best latency but are expensive. Probes are cheaper but may not fully eliminate all cold-paths (trade-off acceptable given cost target).
- Quantized overlays risk small quality regressions on first responses; mitigation is progressive upgrade and quality monitoring tied to eval prompts.
- Synthetic KV priming can bias cache contents; we therefore sample prompts from anonymized requests and maintain per-tenant seed lists to reduce mismatch.

Telemetry / Metrics:
- New metrics: probe_success_rate, probe_duration_ms, probe_load_bytes, probe_memory_delta, kv_hit_rate_post_probe (per-tenant), cold_start_50/95/99.
- Dashboards: visible per-pool and per-tenant for rollout. Alerts if probe failure rate > 5% or memory delta causes OOMs.

Rollout plan:
1) Laboratory PoC on staging with small pool of A100 nodes (done).
2) Canary on internal test tenants (5% traffic) behind feature flag.
3) Measure latency, error rates, and cost impact for 72 hours.
4) Gradual escalations to 25% and 100% if thresholds met.

Testing and validation:
- Load tests simulating tenant mixes (PLG vs enterprise) to validate probe overhead and eviction behavior.
- Regression evals on balanced prompt set to detect quality drop from quantized overlays.
- Chaos tests: kill probes and ensure serving remains stable; force memory pressure to validate probe caps.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- Runtime: add probe mode to weight streamer and expose probe APIs (ENG).
- Fleet controller: add residency scoring and probe orchestration (ENG).
- Autoscaler: ensure probes count toward short-lived capacity without breaking SLA math (ENG/infra).
- Console: dashboards and per-tenant toggle (PM/console).

Notes and links to artifacts: see attachments for PoC results and RFC.
comments: 2026-03-02: Spike completed. PoC shows ~35% reduction in first-token latency for 7B when using mem-prefetch + quantized overlay on staging A100 nodes. Observed small memory churn during simultaneous probes; need caps.

2026-03-04: Design review with Runtime team. Action items: add feature flag, implement sane concurrency limits, annotate probe-generated pages for easier eviction accounting. Runtime owners: @Sofia Martinez, @Oliver Reed.
2026-03-06: PM feedback (Asha): require per-tenant opt-in and clear cost telemetry. Add label and console toggle in Sprint plan.
2026-03-08: Infra note: autoscaler needs to treat probe containers as non-guaranteed compute; otherwise reserved capacity math breaks. Assigned ENG-34790 to infra (dependency).
2026-03-10: Initial implementation PR opened. Waiting on code review for probe orchestration and unit tests. See PR link in attachments.
